articles.title: US Olympic hero Nancy Hogshead launches petition calling for WNBA to restrict gender eligibility
articles.summary: Nancy Hogshead's Change.org petition has over 11,000 signatures demanding the WNBA clarify eligibility rules to explicitly include only biological females.
articles.body: Three-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Nancy Hogshead is calling on the WNBA to explicitly restrict player eligibility to biological females. Hogshead recently launched a Change.org petition asking the league to clarify the meaning of "woman" in its eligibility rules. The petition has collected more than 11,000 signatures since its Aug. 14 launch. "We’re calling for the WNBA to clarify that its eligibility rules are for women only," Hogshead told Fox News Digital. "If you wanna participate, you have to be a certain age, and you have to be a female." CHARLES BARKLEY DECLARES WNBA IS 'FOR WOMEN ONLY' AFTER ONGOING TRANSGENDER ATHLETE DEBATE Hogshead said she hopes the petition ultimately reaches 100,000 signatures. "It’s an 80/20 issue across the country, so we can do it," she said. "We have well over a million people who’ve engaged with our materials that we put out about the petition. We just gotta get them to sign on." The WNBA’s 2026 collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." However, the agreement does not further define "woman" or include specific language addressing gender identity or sex assigned at birth. The debate intensified after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while claiming to identify as women. League sources hav since said that neither of them is eligible and characterized their announcements as "publicity stunts." Hogshead said the declarations exposed what she considers a contradiction in policies based on gender self-identification. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT ON PROTECTING GIRLS FROM COMPETING AGAINST 'BIOLOGICAL MEN' "I love it that they came forward because it just shows the hypocrisy of the WNBA, and it shows the hypocrisy of gender ideology," Hogshead said. "For them to come forward and, you know, threaten to play in the WNBA and show up for the draft, it just shows just how ridiculous that gender ideology is." The WNBA previously said there were "no immediate eligibility matters" affecting the league and denounced "bad-faith efforts" to use the debate to "demean or marginalize others." Commissioner Cathy Engelbert also said league officials would continue discussing the subject with the players’ union and other stakeholders. Hogshead’s petition comes amid rallies outside WNBA games supporting Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who publicly opposed transgender participation in girls’ and women’s sports earlier this summer. "I really appreciate her for the stand that she has taken on behalf of women," Hogshead said of Cunningham. "If anything, the more people see of Sophie Cunningham, the more they like her." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hogshead won three gold medals and one silver medal at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. She later became a civil rights attorney and founded Champion Women, an organization that advocates for women and girls in athletics.

articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors reportedly filled out their roster Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors reportedly filled out their roster Tuesday.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported they agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with Georges Niang. Charania also noted they filled their last two open regular-season roster spots with the additions of Niang and Brandon Williams who "were targeted over the last month for the Warriors and now land on one-year minimum deals."

According to Spotrac , Golden State has $249.4 million in total cap allocations.

SG: Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams, Will Richard

SF: Jimmy Butler (when healthy), Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg

C: Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford, Charles Bassey

Niang surely won't be a go-to option on a roster that includes Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Draymond Green, but he does provide a veteran presence off the bench who can take advantage of openings.

He entered the league as a second-round pick in the 2016 NBA draft and has played for the Indiana Pacers, Utah Jazz, Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers and Atlanta Hawks.

However, the Iowa State product also missed the entire 2025-26 campaign because of a foot injury.

At his best, he is someone who can provide matchup problems for opposing frontcourts because of his outside shooting. Niang is a career 39.9 percent shooter from beyond the arc and connected on 40.6 percent of his triples during the 2024-25 season for the Cavaliers and Hawks on his way to 9.9 points per game.

Given the defensive attention that Curry in particular draws, that should lead to a number of clean looks on the outside for Niang.

His ability to knock them down will ultimately determine how much he plays for a team looking to make a playoff run in the Western Conference.

articles.title: Sky Owner Says Enes Kanter Freedom is Banned From Home Games, Calling Him 'A Potential Threat'
articles.summary: CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever.
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Sky have banned Enes Kanter Freedom from their home games after the former NBA center was ejected from Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever.

Owner Michael Alter made the announcement in a rare news conference on Tuesday. Alter told reporters Freedom is not allowed inside of Wintrust Arena for Sky games "unless sometime in the future, he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat."

The 6-foot-10, 250-pound Freedom was removed from Sunday's game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.

Enes Kanter Freedom Ejected from WNBA Game

Source: Freedom, White Not Eligible for WNBA Draft (AP)

Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Freedom's direction.

Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Freedom, 34, as she approached him. A standing Freedom held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.

"It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and see how much attention he could get," Alter told reporters from the Chicago Sun-Times and other media outlets.

Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.

He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing the arena.

"I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN!" Freedom wrote on social media. "Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told the AP on Monday that they are not eligible. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

articles.title: Watch Penny Hardaway's motivational speech to Memphis football team
articles.summary: Penny Hardaway spoke to the Memphis football team ahead of the 2026 season. Here's what he told them about what it means to play for the Tigers.
articles.body:
Memphis football coach Charles Huff said at his news conference on Aug. 25 that motivational speeches don't mean much once the game actually starts.

But he also said that after Memphis basketball coach Penny Hardaway delivered an impassioned one to the football team about what it means to play at Memphis.

"We carry the city," Hardaway said in a speech that was posted on social media. "We win, it makes our whole entire city better. The people are more happy. The crime goes down, it's already been documented. So when you have that on you, it should mean something. Whether you care about the city of Memphis or not, it should mean something to you. That pride should mean something."

Hardaway would know. He's a Memphis native who played for the Tigers before going to the NBA, eventually returning to Memphis as head basketball coach. He and Huff have built a strong relationship in the time since Huff was hired in December. He already has visited a football practice and said he plans to be around more during the season.

Memphis football has an entirely new coaching staff and a roster made up mostly of transfers. Huff has talked throughout the offseason about using Hardaway to explain to those players what it means to play for the Tigers.

"I was the No. 1 player in the high school rankings," Hardaway said. "I could've went anywhere in the country. I chose to stay home. I didn't choose to stay home because I was a home guy. I chose it because of how the fans made me feel for sure. And that's the same thing that y'all are going to get. You perform at a high level in this city, they treat you like royalty. The reason why is because this thing goes deeper than just tickets to a game. The city will ride with you as long as you're doing what you're supposed to do."

The football team kicks off its season at UNLV on Aug. 29 (9 p.m. CT, FOX). Memphis basketball's season begins on Nov. 2 against Iowa State in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.

In his speech to the team, Hardaway talked about what it means to play for Tigers fans.

"Y'all have to understand: The days you don't want to get up, the days you don't want to do the extra reps, you've got to push all that to the side because that's nothing compared to what these people have to go through every day," he said. "And spend their money to come and watch y'all play."

articles.title: Klay Thompson drops scary Heat & Giannis Antetokounmpo championship proclamation
articles.summary: Klay Thompson knows that the Heat led by Giannis Antetokounmpo are on the road for an NBA championship run and even he dropped a huge promise.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson drops scary Heat & Giannis Antetokounmpo championship proclamation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Just when everyone thought that the Miami Heat were already scary with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo , they got another daunting acquisition. Klay Thompson decided to join the party in South Beach so that he could get a fifth NBA championship under his belt. How confident is the former Dallas Mavericks and Golden State Warriors sharpshooter that he will be able to play at a championship-level once again? Simply put, he is very certain.

Thompson proclaims big championship-level jump to help Antetokounmpo, Heat

Klay Thompson has been far from his championship-caliber form for a while now. The last time that he was able to score more than 20 points on average in the regular season was during the 2022-23 NBA regular season, a year removed from the Warriors' most recent title run. Since then, he has settled for spot-up shooter roles and taught shooting mechanics to younger players on his squads. Thompson aims to change that with the Heat .

He plans to return to form heading into the 2026-27 NBA season and become the perfect complement to Giannis Antetokounmpo. The veteran sharpshooter declared all of this during his introductory press conference.

"I still think I can do it at a high level. Like you said, the durability has been, for me, a huge plus. You know, that's one thing that might have been questioned from all that time I had off. But, for me, all of those injuries are back in the past. I don't even think about them anymore. It's nice to be able to walk on the floor and play free-minded," Thompson declared.

In his most recent season with the Mavericks, Thompson looked like a shell of his former self. He hit a career-low average of 11.7 points while only knocking down 38.3% of his shots from three-point range. Despite that, he has shown strong durability by playing 69 regular-season games, which Antetokounmpo and the Heat could use in the coming season.

In the bigger picture, this move to acquire Thompson makes a lot of sense. With Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. now off the roster, the Heat need someone who can knock down shots. Schematically, Coach Erik Spoelstra has balanced out their inside and outside scoring. This is why the Heat ranked 10th in the league with their 36.4% field goal percentage. With Antetokounmpo joining the Heat, the need to have an elite spot-up shooter has become more apparent. This is because of the gravity the Greek Freak brings when driving inside the paint.

There is still so much to iron out in terms of rotations along with X's and O's. One thing is certain, however: the Heat need Thompson to equal his production from at least that 2022 Warriors NBA Championship run to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy.

articles.title: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run
articles.summary: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run.
articles.body:
In the final week of August, we're in the dog days of summer. Very little is going on in the NBA world. Most of the offseason homework is done and teams are awaiting training camps to start. Right now, everybody is bored out of their mind. But right around the corner, we're about to see the yearly marathon restart.

The Oklahoma City Thunder enter the 2026-27 season as a co-title favorite — alongside the San Antonio Spurs . Even with their cost-cutting moves this offseason, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren should be enough to keep you in the title hunt.

But with Lu Dort and others out the door, Cason Wallace could be in line for a massive promotion. The 22-year-old will likely become a full-time starter this upcoming season. He'll no longer have to call himself the unofficial sixth starter as he has over the first three seasons of his rich basketball career. He'll also get more opportunities to grow on offense.

With a vacuum of possessions and shot attempts up for grabs, Wallace should see an uptick in offensive production. No longer will he have to settle for catch-and-shoot looks with the occasional downhill drive. Now, OKC's success could depend on his development on that side of the floor. It looks like he's taking it seriously this summer.

Wallace showed off his ball-handling creativity in a recent open gym run. He also showed he can pull up from deep outside. In a social media video that highlighted his best plays, he showed some finesse around his driving game as he kissed the ball off the glass for a layup. Everything is set up for him to be a double-digit scorer for the first time in his career this upcoming season. It's now about running away with that opportunity.

These summer months are when NBA players usually make the most strides in their respective games. The downtime allows them to work on their craft undisturbed. It'll be interesting to see how Wallace looks as he's about to enter his fourth NBA season already.

articles.summary: Lonzo Ball revealed that LaMelo Ball has a driver to help with his many road situations after buying $1 million cars and finding ways to damage them.
articles.body: LaMelo Ball’s extensive car collection has drawn attention since his rise to basketball stardom. But the Minnesota Timberwolves guard has now decided to employ a personal driver to help him get around his new NBA home, according to his older brother, Lonzo Ball. During a recent edition of the "Curious Mike" podcast, Lonzo Ball pointed to his younger brother while discussing which member of the Ball family spends the most money with Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. "Who in your family out of y'all three spends the most [money]," Porter asked. "The one who has the most, LaMelo," Lonzo replied. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "[He's] got 10 cars," Lonzo continued. Having a driver could mean the 25-year-old spends less time behind the wheel and, in turn, has fewer opportunities to be involved in an accident. Lonzo also suggested LaMelo could benefit from choosing vehicles outside the exotic-car category, rather than Lamborghinis and similar high-performance models he has owned in the past. LAMELO BALL'S CUSTOM HUMMER LOSES WHEEL IN CHARLOTTE CRASH DURING ALL-STAR BREAK "He'll buy a $1 million car and then just immediately f–k it up, I've never understood [that]," Lonzo added in reference to his sibling's habits when it comes to vehicles. "You just bought that? And then you ripped it up? You could've just got a beater," the former Los Angeles Lakers guard noted. Lonzo then addressed the perception surrounding the frequency of LaMelo’s road incidents, saying his younger brother "doesn’t get into accidents, but he has a lot of situations on the road." The Lakers selected Lonzo Ball with the second overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. He later played for the New Orleans Pelicans and Chicago Bulls before joining the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2025. The Cavaliers traded him to the Utah Jazz in February 2026, but the Jazz subsequently waived him before he appeared in a game for the team. Lonzo's NBA career has been marked by injuries. After appearing in 35 games during the 2021-22 season, he spent more than two calendar years sidelined. "It was like a 1,000 and something days," Ball said, reflecting on the length of his absence. He added that he has come to terms with the possibility that he may not return to the same level he once reached as an athlete. "I came at peace with that when I got hurt the first time. Every time you get hurt it kind of sets you back," Ball told Porter. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Hornets selected LaMelo with the third overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. She has done so by putting up unprecedented combination statistics that highlight both her elite scoring and her generational passing.

articles.title: College athletics' latest mess: Court orders say athletes can play, but SEC and Big Ten ready to fight
articles.summary: The SEC and Big Ten voted to bar athletes with pro sports experience, but attorney Ryan Downton says the move violates multiple court orders.
articles.body: The college athletics world is reeling after the SEC and Big Ten created new guidelines governing the eligibility of athletes who planned to join teams this week following injunctions and temporary restraining orders granted by multiple judges. On Tuesday, both conferences, who will soon be joined by the ACC and Big 12, voted to enact new rules that would prevent athletes who have participated in professional sports from reentering the college landscape. The decision comes after players in several states were granted injunctions or temporary restraining orders allowing them to play this season. Most of the lawsuits stem from the NCAA’s new eligibility guidelines, which give athletes five years to play five seasons of college athletics. NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME Conference guidelines prohibit players from NFL, NBA or WNBA Under the new policies, any athlete who has signed with a professional team, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition. But, there was one difference from a public standpoint with the SEC and Big Ten. On Tuesday evening, SEC presidents and chancellors held a vote on how to move forward with the new guidelines pertaining to these ongoing cases revolving around athletes who have participated at the professional level in some form or fashion. NCAA IGNORED THE WARNINGS. NOW IT'S FIGHTING FOR SURVIVAL IN COURTROOMS ACROSS AMERICA OVER ELIGIBILITY In addition to the guidelines created by the SEC, the conference has also given Greg Sankey the power to enforce these rules, which include suspension of coaches and monetary fines to each school who violates them. So, what does this mean for schools who are preparing to bring athletes onto campus for the upcoming college football or basketball season? According to attorney Ryan Downton, who represents a number of players, the are currently "working on a legal strategy" on how to move forward against both the NCAA and participating conferences who have enacted these new guidelines. "The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," Downton told OutKick-Fox News on Tuesday night. "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level" OLE MISS FILES LAWSUITS AGAINST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYERS WHO LEFT FOR LANE KIFFIN'S LSU Multiple sources told OutKick that the vote within the SEC was unanimous, though that does not mean there will not be legal action taken over the next few days. "We are still working on a legal strategy," attorney Ryan Downton noted. Abide by court orders or violate conference guidelines? Decisions upcoming At the forefront of this fight, even though he was not the first coach or team to bring in a player who has in some way competed at the NFL level, is LSU coach Lane Kiffin. Over the last few days, Kiffin has voiced his reasoning behind the recruitment of such athletes who have already gained NFL experience. Essentially, the Tigers coach mentioned that if he didn’t strike first, some other school would. "So, you know, we have you know made a decision to recruit some kids around the country, and through these multiple injunctions around the country, which, this is not a first time in college sports, a group of players were granted a fifth year of eligibility, in multiple sports. And through them winning their injunction and entry into the portal, they’re available to recruit," Kiffin noted on Monday. "So ourselves, like many places around the country, are recruiting them. At the end of the day, you know, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country. So, we made a decision to recruit them, like probably most people are." This includes former Ole Miss football players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who are both set to join the LSU roster thanks to a ruling from the 19th District Court of Louisiana that granted them an additional season of eligibility. But, there have been plenty of others who have gone down this route, winning cases in state courts that allow them to return this season. Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson is another, who sued the NCAA in a Texas court for an additional season. Attorney Darren Heitner, who represents Dae'Quan Wright, told OutKick that the SEC should abide by the order granted by the 19th District Court of Louisiana. "He should be rostered by LSU and be a great contributor for the Tigers. The SEC should heed the court order recently issued by a Louisiana judge," Heitner said. The question is whether LSU, and others, will move forward in bringing in athletes knowing that it would be in violation of conference rules, but also legal in the eyes of the courts who have granted them injunctions. The Dallas Wings are heading to the WNBA playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Dallas clinched a spot in the 2026 postseason Tuesday with a 96-78 win over the Portland Fire. The Wings clinched the final playoff spot, meaning the Fire have been eliminated from postseason contention.

Now that the Wings are officially in, their attention will turn toward the battle for seeding. They are currently in eighth place in the WNBA standings and playoff picture

The eighth seed will play the first seed in the first round of the WNBA playoff bracket, meaning Dallas could be in store for a showdown against the Minnesota Lynx if the current playoff position holds.

Dallas making the playoffs represents one of the most impressive turnarounds in recent league history, as it was an ugly 10-34 last season and 9-31 during the 2024 campaign. It ended up with the first overall pick of the 2025 and 2026 WNBA drafts, and it turned to UConn's backcourt each time as it built the foundation for a contender.

Paige Bueckers wasted little time establishing herself as one of the WNBA's biggest stars after the Wings took her with the first pick in 2025. She captured the Rookie of the Year and was an All-WNBA Second Team selection as a bright spot for a struggling club.

Dallas then gave her a familiar teammate when it selected Azzi Fudd with the first pick in this year's draft. While Fudd hasn't been quite as dominant as Bueckers, she provided immediate shooting on the wing and remains one of the best in the league from long distance.

Playing alongside Bueckers certainly makes life easier for her and the rest of the Wings, as the guard draws plenty of defensive attention and creates openings for all of her teammates. She was once again an All-Star in her second season and has taken a leap to become an even more dominant playmaker.

In fact, she has remained in MVP discussions for much of the season, and an All-WNBA First Team selection would be anything but a surprise.

While Bueckers has been the driving force behind Dallas' turnaround with Fudd providing important secondary contributions, it hasn't all been about the youth movement.

Veterans Arike Ogunbowale and Jessica Shepard have made their presence felt with leadership and much-needed offense. They are each averaging better than 14 points a night, while Shepard is a double-double threat every time she steps on the floor.

Her inside presence provides balance and offensive versatility, which helps the Wings make opponents pay when they focus too much on the perimeter with Bueckers and the wing with Ogunbowale.

The Wings may be a season or two ahead of schedule with such a dramatic turnaround, but they are a threat to anyone in the playoffs with a superstar like Bueckers who can take over at a moment's notice and a solid supporting cast in place.

Two days later, Sky owner Michael Alter made it official: Freedom is no longer welcome at Wintrust Arena.Enes Kanter Freedom faces first WNBA arena banAlter said the club would only reconsider "if he's able to prove to us he's able to abide by our rules." That single line drew the hardest boundary of the whole saga: not a suspension, not a warning, but an outright ban from the building.The trouble started late in the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Indiana Fever. Freedom was sitting baseline in a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. adult human female."Cloud, fresh off a bucket and a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly, walked straight at him, yelling and pointing. Security still walked him out.On his way through the lobby, Freedom spun around, held his shirt out toward the crowd, and talked to a group of police officers before he left the building. He later posted on social media that he'd been "kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN."The league itself had reportedly planned to let the incident pass without punishment, since Freedom never actually stepped onto the playing surface. Alter clearly saw it differently. Freedom and fellow former NBA player Royce White have both declared for the WNBA draft on the same grounds, though a person familiar with the league's thinking told the AP that neither is considered eligible. One fan summed up the mood with a simple "What has the world come to ð."Others leaned into mockery: "Now he can go back to begging the boys at the rec center to choose him for a pickup game." Smith weighed in with his usual mix of sympathy and scolding. He credited Freedom's history of standing up to the Turkish government but said stepping toward Cloud was "excessive," adding that the WNBA players themselves "don't deserve" to be caught in the middle of a fight that belongs with the league, not the roster.âIt was a classless thing for him to do because it's not the ladies that are playing don't have anything to do with this. articles.title: Wings clinch final WNBA playoff spot with win over Fire as seeding battle continues
articles.summary: The eight team field for the WNBA playoffs is now set.
articles.body:
The Dallas Wings picked up a 96-78 win over the Portland Fire on Tuesday night at the Moda Center, a victory that officially locked up the eighth and final postseason spot this summer. The Wings are in the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

The loss eliminated the Fire from playoff contention. The expansion team entered Tuesday night more than six games back from the Wings in the standings, so the outcome was very likely expected.

While the playoff field is now solidified, no seed has been locked up yet. The Minnesota Lynx hold the best record in the league and are on pace to grab the No. 1 seed. They could have clinched that seed on Monday night , but fell to the Golden State Valkyries , who are second in the league standings.

As seeding plays out over the last several weeks of the regular season, here are the eight teams who will have a shot at claiming the WNBA title later this fall:

Minnesota Lynx Golden State Valkyries Las Vegas Aces Atlanta Dream Indiana Fever New York Liberty Washington Mystics Dallas Wings

The WNBA playoffs will start on Sept. 27.

The Wings took a 50-37 lead at halftime after leading nearly the entire way in the first half against the Fire on Tuesday night. They then opened the third quarter on a 15-4 tear to break the game wide open and cruised to the 18-point win.

Paige Bueckers led the way with 22 points and 11 assists while shooting 8-of-15 from the field in the win. Jessica Shepard added 21 points and nine rebounds.

The Wings, with five games left in the regular season, now sit at 23-16 on the year. The 23 victories is the most the team has won in a single campaign since it relocated to Dallas in 2016.

While the Wings are the final team to land a playoff berth, they entered Tuesday less than three games out of fifth. It will take a big push, and a bit of help, but there is still room for Bueckers and the Wings to make a run and improve their postseason spot.

articles.title: "A dirty play, period" NBA Hall of Famer makes big WNBA claim involving Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham
articles.summary: NBA News: Charles Barkley does not hesitate to tiptoe around a topic, and recently, the WNBA's roughest stretch of the season gave him plenty to swing at. Talki.
articles.body: Charles Barkley does not hesitate to tiptoe around a topic, and recently, the WNBA's roughest stretch of the season gave him plenty to swing at. Talking through the league's ugliest recent headlines, the Hall of Famer landed on a claim that had nothing to do with basketball skill and everything to do with why two of the league's biggest names keep drawing so much heat from their peers.The comments came on The Michael Smerconish Program, where Barkley and the host spent time picking apart what Barkley called the WNBA's "awful year." Barkleyâs comment stems from DiJonai Carrington's hard foul on Sophie Cunningham.Charles Barkley drops unexpected take on Caitlin Clark and Sophie CunninghamThe foul itself happened on Aug. 8, when DiJonai Carrington caught Sophie Cunningham in the head during a fast break, leaving her with a bloody mouth. Officials reviewed it and upgraded the call to a Flagrant 2, ejecting Carrington from the game.What turned a rough basketball play into a national story was what came next. Carrington posted "WHITE PRIVILEGE" on social media shortly after, tagging the Fever, then later said she never meant the foul itself was about race without clarifying what she did mean.Barkley wasn't interested in overthinking the play. "A dirty play. Period," he said, brushing aside any attempt to complicate what he saw as a simple hard foul. He argued Carrington's post, not the contact, is what dragged race into a conversation that started on the court."When you turn stuff to the internet, all the race hustlers start coming out. We have a ton of race hustlers out there, White and Black. Let me repeat that. White and Black," Barkley said.Charles Barkley explains why he thinks WNBA stars hate Caitlin Clark and Sophie CunninghamBarkley stopped short of calling anyone in the league racist, saying flatly he had no proof for that kind of claim. But he didn't shy away from a theory of his own for why Clark and Cunningham draw so much friction from other players. He pointed to a mix of factors rather than one single cause, saying he couldn't begin to sort out how much each one mattered."Those girls do not like Caitlin Clark or Sophie Cunningham. Without regard for race, they just donât like them," Barkley shared."Sheâs just a really good basketball player. Same thing with Sophie. Sheâs a good player. I think it has something to do with se*uality, race, and jealousy. I think itâs all three of them. I donât know how you break up the percentages."The league is growing, players are earning more under a new labor deal, and there's a wave of young talent that should be the story. Instead, he said, the headlines keep circling back to hard fouls and social media fights instead of the games themselves. âI donât think it works like that anymore, Michael. Whenâs the last time you heard something positive about the WNBA? I canât even remember."Colin Cowherd compares Caitlin Clark to Michael Jordan and Stephen CurryWhile Barkley was dissecting the WNBA's off-court drama, Colin Cowherd was busy handing out one of the boldest comparisons Clark has received all year. On "The Herd," Cowherd described her as a blend of two of basketball's most decorated names, pointing to her refusal to engage with any of the noise surrounding her as proof of a Jordan-like mindset layered onto Curry-level scoring range.Cowherd backed the praise with numbers, noting Clark's status among the league leaders in assists and scoring while running what he called the best offense in WNBA history. Clark is averaging 22.1 points, 8.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds a game this season, numbers that have kept her firmly in the MVP conversation as Indiana heads toward the playoffs. articles.title: RJ Luis Jr. cleared by judge to play for LSU after spending time with 2 NBA teams
articles.summary: Former St. John’s standout RJ Luis Jr. has been cleared by a court to start practicing with LSU and potentially play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season.

Luis, who briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics but never played in an NBA game, hugged LSU coach Will Wade after the ruling by East Baton Rouge Parish District Court judge Ronald R. Johnson.

After a five-hour hearing, Johnson granted the player's request for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which had argued Luis was unlikely to win reinstatement after leaving college to turn pro in 2025.

"This is precedent. It's monumental," said Baton Rouge-based attorney Tony Clayton, who represented Luis along with Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina. "This allows him to go practice, go play and we'll let the legal process work itself out."

The timeline for that process was not immediately clear.

"I don't know, but there's a lot of discovery that Elliot and I have to obtain," Clayton said. "We've got a lot of questions."

Luis' attorneys noted that the NCAA had granted exceptions allowing numerous players from overseas professional leagues to join college basketball programs, and argued that American players must be afforded the same opportunity.

They stressed that Luis not only had never played in an NBA game, but also had not played for the Celtics' G League affiliate because of an injury, and had far less of a professional basketball resume than numerous college players who'd been recruited from abroad.

NCAA attorney Taylor Askew argued that Luis' situation was not comparable to those who played for the developmental squads of pro organizations overseas because Luis chose to leave college for the NBA.

Askew noted that the only player in a similar situation to Luis was Alabama's Charles Bediako, who won a temporary retraining order allowing him to play five games for Alabama last season before an Alabama judge ultimately sided with NCAA assertions that he was ineligible.

"I understand Mr. Luis is disappointed that he was not drafted and did not play in the NBA as much as he would have liked," Askew said. "Actions have consequences. Decisions have outcomes and they're not always the right ones or the ones that you want."

As he made his ruling, Johnson said, "In the court's mind, (Luis) did not actually play professional basketball," and that whether Luis was properly advised of his options at the time he left college "lingers heavily before this court."

Great Britain's men's basketball team have turned to the NBA in their bid to progress into the full qualifying rounds for the 2029 EuroBasket campaign.

The side, led by Newcastle Eagles head coach Marc Steutel, has been able to name three players in his squad who are either current or recent players in the world's top domestic league for this week's double-header against Switzerland and Slovakia.

Boston Celtics centre Amari Williams is part of the squad, as is power forward Tobi Lawal who was drafted by the Dallas Mavericks earlier this summer.

Another addition to what is, on paper, the strongest GB squad in some time is forward Tosan Evbuomwan. The 25-year-old has this summer joined Barcelona following three seasons in the NBA and its reserve G-League.

"With every squad selection, you want to try to make sure that you are getting the balance of the most talented players available," Steutel told BBC Sport.

"Because of where our players play and the restrictions that has at times, it's not always as straightforward on the outside as people may think.

"We feel really excited about this group for sure."

The trio make up three quarters of the four most recent British players to feature in the league, alongside OG Anunoby of the New York Knicks.

Great Britain enter the second of three preliminary qualifying rounds for the 2029 EuroBasket tournament. They face both Switzerland and Slovakia home and away across three international windows in August, November and February.

Should GB finish top of the group, they will enter full qualifying for EuroBasket. Failure to do so will see them enter the final round of preliminary qualifying next year.

How have GB been able to land NBA players?

For Evbuomwan and Williams, 24, this double-header on Thursday in Switzerland and then at home to Slovakia in Newcastle on Sunday is set to mark their GB debuts at senior level.

But how the duo have been able to sign up for the latest fixtures is all about timing.

Four of GB's six first-round qualifying matches for the 2027 Fiba World Cup were in November 2025 and March 2026, which clashed with the NBA season.

But with this window opening in between NBA seasons, as well as those of its European counterparts, the stars aligned for Steutel and his team.

"In the season, guys in the NBA [and] the EuroLeague, we struggle to get. There's very little ability to be able to do that," added Steutel.

"We're right before the start of the season and our general manager has done an incredible job communicating with the Boston Celtics. Tosan is closer to home now with Barcelona.

"They've both been really supportive and want those guys to play, so [we're] really excited."

GB's coaching staff have long craved the opportunity to be able to cash in by adding recent NBA players to their squad.

Dan Clark, who featured at the 2012 Olympics alongside two-time NBA All-Star Luol Deng, is now GB's general manager and has stayed in contact with Newcastle-born Evbuomwan and Williams, awaiting the opportunity to be able to call on the duo.

"It's not just a 'this window' thing, it has taken years," explains Steutel.

"Tosan is someone who I've known for a long time and I've followed his journey. He's someone who has communicated really well with us and Amari likewise. Dan Clark has been communicating with Amari for years.

"We're able to get the timing right now and get them in a GB jersey. It's great for the team, but I think it's great for British basketball on the whole."

'To have our debuts at the same time is special'

While the journeys of Williams and Evbuomwan from English upbringings to reaching the NBA have differed in some ways, the crux of their stories is the same.

A school year apart, Evbuomwan moved to Princeton University in New Jersey in 2019. A year later, Williams made a similar move to attend Drexel University in Philadelphia.

Both were starting their basketball journeys that would ultimately tee up their senior international debuts.

"It was something I've been trying to do since I moved away to America seven years ago," said the Nottingham-born Williams, who was drafted by Orlando Magic in 2025 and traded to the Celtics.

"To have the opportunity to do it this summer is something I've been looking forward to ."

Evbuomwan added: "It's exciting. All of us being able to commit to this window.

"Me and Amari talk a lot and it is something we have talked about for a while. For us to have both our debuts at the same time in the same window is special."

There is an added homecoming for Evbuomwan when GB face Slovakia on Sunday. It is being played at the Vertu Arena in Newcastle, the home venue of the Eagles, for whom he previously played at youth level.

Evbuomwan added: "Very meaningful. Being able to represent your country is one thing. Being able to represent your country in front of your family and friends is a bonus."

'We'd love to see Anunoby in a GB jersey' - Steutel

Across the three international windows in August, November and March, Great Britain, Slovakia and Switzerland will each get a window each of playing two matches.

GB have theirs this week and will want to take advantage of the star power available to them before the domestic season restarts.

But moving forward, there is another name Steutel and his supporting cast would love to add in OG Anunoby.

The 29-year-old was a key man for the New York Knicks as they won their first NBA title in more than half a century in June.

A two-time NBA winner, Anunoby is also eligible for the United States and Nigeria, having yet to play international basketball for any nation at senior level.

Great Britain remain hopeful of one day getting the London-born forward in their ranks.

"Our general manager is in communication with OG and his team," said Steutel.

"His season went way into the summer, winning the championship and playing a lot of basketball. Unfortunately, the timing is not right on this window - but we hope so.

"Our qualification now is for EuroBasket 2029 and we hope we can get there. It is a long way away. But he's someone else we'd definitely love to see in a GB jersey."

articles.summary: The WNBA had high expectations for its product after securing a historic collective bargaining agreement in the spring, and while there have been a plethora...
articles.body:
Mercury news: Phoenix-Mystics clash paused after sex toy gets thrown onto court appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The WNBA had high expectations for its product after securing a historic collective bargaining agreement in the spring, and while there have been a plethora of notable achievements from both a team and individual perspective, media coverage continues to revolve around non-game story lines. That trend continued during Tuesday night's battle between the Phoenix Mercury and Washington Mystics . A fan dampened the excitement surrounding Kelsey Plum's home debut in the Mortgage Matchup Center.

Once again, a sex toy was hurled onto the court during a WNBA game. This latest incident occurred in the final few minutes of the first half, forcing the action into a brief pause. Boos echoed the arena. The object was quickly removed from the area, and so was the perpetrator, per Eliav Gabay of Sports360AZ.

The Chicago Sky experienced the same migraine in Friday night's home game versus the Golden State Valkyrie. Players and coaches have had enough . Safety is always a concern when items are thrown, but it is also about the message that is being sent. Simply put, these women are being disrespected.

Although Phoenix (13-25) did its best to flip the headlines back to basketball, the struggling squad could not overpower the visiting Mystics (23-15). Alyssa Thomas posted a double-double with three steals, Natasha Mack totaled 19 points, eight rebounds, three blocks and three steals of her own and Kahleah Copper added 19 points, but the Mercury still suffered a 94-84 loss in The Desert.

Plum scored 10 points on just 4-of-12 shooting. Foul trouble limited her to 17 minutes of game time. Needless to say, it was not the first impression she wanted to make in Phoenix. The Mystics trio of Sonia Citron , Kiki Iriafen and Shakira Austin efficiently combined for 53 points in the victory.

Ultimately, a significant amount of focus will be placed on the sex toy disruption. The WNBA should be running out of patience.

articles.title: Peyton Watson Shares Heartfelt Message to Nuggets Fans
articles.summary: Former Denver Nuggets swingman Peyton Watson shared a heartfelt message with Nuggets fans after leaving the team in free agency.After spending the first four...
articles.body:
Former Denver Nuggets swingman Peyton Watson shared a heartfelt message with Nuggets fans after leaving the team in free agency.

After spending the first four seasons of his NBA career in Denver, Watson signed a four-year, $88 million deal with the Cleveland Cavaliers as part of a sign-and-trade deal involving five teams.

In return for Watson, the Nuggets received a first-round pick and a second-round pick.

While it was no doubt tough for the Nuggets to let Watson go, the reality of the NBA's second apron made it difficult for Denver to keep him on the roster unless they were willing to go deep into the punitive second apron to do so.

Peyton Watson Shares Statement With Nuggets Fans

Now that Watson is officially on Cleveland's roster, he shared a heartfelt statement with Nuggets fans after leaving the only fanbase that he's ever known during his NBA career.

"Nuggets Nation and the city of Denver, Thank you for having me for the first four years of my career. As a young NBA player, who was a bit naive and hadn't seen much of the real world, you guys took care of me better than I could have ever imagined. Thanks for that. Playing this game every night on the national stage is difficult on both the body and the mind, but the love from the fans always makes it so worthwhile. I will miss seeing you all at Ball Arena. A few special thank yous: Calvin Booth for believing in me out of UCLA. The Kroenke family. Coach Malone, Coach Adelman and the rest of the staff. All of my teammates for helping to raise me up. AG for being my big brother. DJ for keeping me in check. Joker and Jamal for all the assists on and off the floor. KCP for throwing my 21st birthday party. MPJ for all the late night workouts and dinners. But again, most of all, thank you to the fans. Playing in front of you has been a dream come true. I'll see you all soon.P-Wat," Watson wrote on his Instagram .

Now that Watson is a member of the Cavaliers' roster, the Nuggets have already moved on, as the team has signed DeMar DeRozan to a one-year, $3.9 million veteran's minimum contract to fill in for Watson's minutes next season.

Though DeRozan is 37 years old , he is still a quality player and one who can still get a bucket when the team needs it. He is also much cheaper than Watson, whose contract starts at $20.5 million next season, while DeRozan comes in at just $3.9 million.

With the Nuggets the only NBA team currently over the second apron, every dollar counts, so had they kept Watson on the team's roster, they would have been paying tens of millions more in luxury tax penalties. Now that he's gone and replaced with DeRozan, the team is only a few million over the second apron and can potentially even get under it if they trade someone like veteran Zeke Nnaji in a salary dump.

articles.title: Angel Reese beats Caitlin Clark to WNBA Player of the Week honours alongside A’ja Wilson
articles.summary: Angel Reese just had one of the best weeks of her WNBA career, and has been rewarded for it after being named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week. Ange...
articles.body:
Angel Reese just had one of the best weeks of her WNBA career, and has been rewarded for it after being named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week.

Angel Reese has been on a run to shut all her haters up in this past week. The Atlanta Dream went 3-0 during the week before this, beating the Aces, the Sparks, and the Mercury.

Reese was immense during these clashes, averaging 24.0 points, 11.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists. She shot an incredible 69 percent from the field during this stretch too.

The Dream star is currently chasing the highest possible seed for the playoffs alongside her teammates. Her rival Caitlin Clark is doing the same with the Indiana Fever , but Reese's efforts have received rewards over CC's in week 13 of the season.

The key reason Angel Reese likely won Player of the Week over Caitlin Clark

Clark averaged 23.0 points, 8.3 assists and 3.5 rebounds herself during this stretch, setting some WNBA records in the process, too. Some fans felt that she should have been named Player of the Week.

However, the W announced that the award was going to Reese, alongside Las Vegas star A'ja Wilson. And there is one key difference between the weeks the two young superstars had.

Reese and Clark may have comparable stats individually, however team results tell a different story. While the Dream had a perfect record during the week, the Indiana Fever went 2-2 in four games.

Helping her team to wins is likely what got Angel the award over her rival. She's not looking back either, the 24-year-old immediately set the WNBA record for most rebounds in a single game to follow up this stretch.

With the Dream and the Fever both set to make the playoffs, a matchup between the two at the highest level is looking like a very real possibility. The rivalry is heating up once again, and it's hard to imagine anything more exciting as a WNBA fan.

articles.title: Preocupación por la salud mental del exACB Kyle Singler
articles.standfirst: El exjugador vuelve a publicar vídeos en los que dice que su vida corre peligro y ataca a Mike Krzyzewski, su antiguo entrenador en Duke
articles.summary: El exjugador vuelve a publicar vídeos en los que dice que su vida corre peligro y ataca a Mike Krzyzewski, su antiguo entrenador en Duke
articles.body: La salud mental del exjugador Kyle Singler vuelve a ser motivo de preocupación después de que la publicación en su cuenta de Instagram de unos vídeos en los que se le puede ver con aspecto desaliñado arremetiendo contra el legendario entrenador Mike Krzyzewski, que le dirigió en la Universidad de Duke. También asegura que ha habido gente que ha entrado en su casa, le ha robado dinero y le ha manipulado sus cuentas bancarias. En un lenguaje a veces ininteligible, se escucha a Singler decir que su antiguo entrenador le ha tendido "una trampa" y le ha "abandonado". El alero, que tiene 38 años, fue el jugador más destacado en el título universitario que Duke conquistó en 2010 con Coach K en el banquillo. "Entrenador, ¿dónde está? Pensé que estábamos en el mismo equipo", se le escucha. El exjugador afirma sentirse prisionero: "Estoy encerrado en mi casa y ya no tengo libertad". Sus cuentas bancarias, según dice, están congeladas y le han cortado hasta la luz de un domicilio en el que se siente "prisionero". Lo más preocupante es cuando Singler confiesa: "Mi vida corre peligro". No es la primera vez que lo dice. En noviembre de 2024, ya publicó un vídeo en el que afirmaba haber sido maltratado y temía por su vida. Entonces, el sindicato de jugadores de la NBA se puso en contacto con su familia y jugadores como Kevin Love, Isaiah Thomas y Andre Drummond le ofrecieron su apoyo públicamente. "Te quiero, Kyle. Escríbeme cuando quieras, por favor", escribió el primero de ellos. Singler, estrella universitaria, tuvo una primera experiencia profesional en el Lucentum Alicante. Después firmó por el Real Madrid, donde estuvo en la temporada 2011-12. Los Pistons le abrieron las puertas de la NBA y también jugó en los Thunder. Tras seis temporadas en Estados Unidos regresaría a España para enrolarse en el Obradoiro y disputar dos encuentros con La Laguna Tenerife en 2019.

articles.title: Llull: "No echo la vista atrás. Es como si fuera mi primera temporada"
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Real Madrid, cerca de los 39 años y a punto de iniciar su vigésima campaña en el club, analiza el próximo curso
articles.summary: El capitán del Real Madrid, cerca de los 39 años y a punto de iniciar su vigésima campaña en el club, analiza el próximo curso
articles.body: El escolta y capitán del Real Madrid, Sergio Llull, dijo este martes que su propósito para esta nueva temporada es "ayudar" al equipo y "ser un ejemplo" en el día a día para los jugadores nuevos y los más jóvenes. A punto de cumplir 39 años, Llull amplió su contrato hasta el final de la temporada 2026-2027 con el Real Madrid y cumplirá su vigésima campaña en el club blanco, del que es el jugador con más partidos disputados en la historia. "Las sensaciones son muy buenas, ha venido todo el mundo en forma y están siendo semanas duras de pretemporada, es lo que toca ahora y contento de empezar otra temporada más", señaló el jugador de Mahón (Mallorca) en declaraciones a Real Madrid TV. Los objetivos del equipo son "intentar llegar a las finales de todas las competiciones que disputemos e intentar ganarlas. Ese es el objetivo global y a corto plazo, adaptarnos todos a los jugadores nuevos y ellos a lo que es el Real Madrid", destacó. Sobre el nuevo entrenador del equipo, Pedro Martínez, resaltó: "Tiene un estilo de juego muy dinámico, con una defensa agresiva y es algo que puede venir bien para los jugadores que tenemos y al equipo". Llull afronta su vigésima temporada en el Real Madrid y prefiere "no mirar atrás" y "pensar" que es la primera, por lo que "intentará" jugar al cien por cien para "inspirar" a los nuevos jugadores, al igual que Felipe Reyes y Rudy Fernández hicieron con él. articles.summary: With Klay Thompson joining the Miami Heat, fans couldn’t help but draw a comparison to Ray Allen, the sharpshooter who won his second NBA title after moving...
articles.body:
With Klay Thompson joining the Miami Heat , fans couldn't help but draw a comparison to Ray Allen , the sharpshooter who won his second NBA title after moving to South Beach ahead of the 2012-13 season.

On Tuesday, Thompson was asked to comment on this comparison when he appeared on ESPN West Palm. In the radio interview, the four-time NBA champion said he was flattered by all the Allen chatter.

"Of course I like those comparisons. I love Ray Allen. Are you kidding me? Him and Reggie were the blueprint for my whole off ball formula. It gives me chills I'm even in the same sentence as Ray, because if you told me this my rookie season, I would've never believed you."

Expressing his astonishment at being likened to Allen, Thompson invoked the memory of the Hall of Famer's greatest moment in a Heat uniform.

"Ray has one of the greatest shots, obviously, in NBA history. I still practice that drill, that back pedal drill to the corner, like he did in Game 6 in 2013."

Thompson was referring to the moment when Allen caught a pass off a Chris Bosh offensive board and hit a corner three to send Game 6 of the 2013 NBA Finals into overtime. The Heat went on to win that night to force Game 7, eventually claiming the NBA championship at the expense of the San Antonio Spurs .

Thompson, who is chasing his fifth title, will be a designated shooter to space the floor for his All-Star teammates Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

"We Got a Great History Together": Klay Thompson Talks About Reuniting With Former Warriors Teammate Andrew Wiggins

Klay Thompson may take some time to get used to calling Miami his NBA home, but there is a familiar face who can help him get settled in the locker room.

In his introductory press conference on Tuesday, Thompson talked about reconnecting with Andrew Wiggins, a teammate of his on the 2022 Golden State Warriors championship squad.

"Andrew was the first one to talk to me, cause I think he's the only one who had my cell phone number. It was good to talk to Wigs. We got a great history together. Winning a championship together was really awesome."

Thompson added that Wiggins, who was dealt to the Heat in last year's Jimmy Butler trade, made his job in Golden State easier because he was "such a great defender."

articles.title: 5 NBA Trade Candidates Nobody Is Talking About
articles.summary: This offseason's list of trade candidates was well known.
articles.body:
This offseason's list of trade candidates was well known.

Giannis Antetokounmpo. Ja Morant. Kawhi Leonard. All have since been moved. Well, in Leonard's case, kind of.

We're still roughly a month away from training camps opening up, however, giving us time for some more potential trades.

There are some obvious stars and starters out there who could still be on the trade block that everyone seems to be overlooking, either because their teams have been quiet this summer or have already pulled off attention-grabbing headlines.

The following five players could be available for the right price and could be moved before the start of the 2026-27 regular season, yet have largely flown under the radar.

It was easy to overlook Ty Jerome last season. The veteran guard was limited to just 15 games following various injuries and the Memphis Grizzlies were shifting to a rebuild by trading away Jaren Jackson Jr. at the deadline and Desmond Bane the summer before.

When he was on the floor, however, Jerome was one of the biggest offensive threats in the NBA.

The 29-year-old guard averaged a career-high 19.7 points, 5.7 assists and shot 42.0 percent from three in just 22.6 minutes per game. To put this in context, Jerome ranked No. 7 overall in the NBA in points per 100 possessions (41.2), putting him ahead of players like Kevin Durant, Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Maxey, Donovan Mitchell and almost every other top scorer.

Unlike these other players, Jerome will be far easier for contenders to trade for.

Entering the second season of a three-year, $27.7 million contract he signed with Memphis last offseason, Jerome is owed a very reasonable $9.2 million in 2026-27. He plays a fearless brand of basketball, is an outstanding shooter and has the feistiness that coaches and teammates love.

Assuming he's 100 percent healthy now, Jerome should be a hot name on the trade market for teams who need a backup point guard who can run an offense or play alongside a floor general as a scoring guard. The defense is suspect, although few players are slowing down Jerome on the other end, either.

Some franchise is going to get a bargain if it can swoop in and acquire Jerome from the young Grizzlies, as he's an immediate plug-and-play rotation option.

Scoot Henderson, G, Portland Trail Blazers

Scoot Henderson already faced an uncertain role with the Portland Trail Blazers this season given the return of Damian Lillard from a torn Achilles. The trade for Ja Morant only further complicates things.

Morant, Lillard and veteran Jrue Holiday are all going to be ahead of Henderson on the depth chart. Portland also has to find minutes for wing Shaedon Sharpe, who averaged a career-high 20.8 points per game last season.

Henderson is also entering the final year of his rookie-scale contract, making him a low-risk trade candidate for teams that want to explore the former No. 3 overall pick's upside while he's still on a rookie deal.

A muscular, athletic guard who can attack downhill, Henderson is still a mystery box at this point. Is he more like the player who averaged 23.3 points and shot 52.2 percent from three in the first two games of the playoffs against the San Antonio Spurs? Or more like the version who put up just 2.5 points on 15.4 percent shooting overall in Games 3 and 4?

The outside shot has been inconsistent throughout his young career, as injuries and a roller coaster role have limited the 22-year-old's ability to break out.

The Blazers should be happy to flip him for some wing depth, given the amount of guards now on this roster.

The Memphis Grizzlies, oddly enough, make sense as a trade partner given that Morant is now in Portland. The Dallas Mavericks are looking for young stars to pair with Cooper Flagg and the Golden State Warriors could be a sneaky destination for Henderson to play a backup role behind Stephen Curry.

A one-year, $13.5 million contract is easy to absorb for teams willing to take a chance on Henderson's upside.

Lauri Markkanen was a hot name on the trade market in recent years. This offseason? Crickets.

This could be because the Utah Jazz finally look like they could become contenders. An aggressive trade for Jaren Jackson Jr. at the deadline combined with the selection of Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 overall pick in the draft has this franchise set up well for the next several years.

This is also why Markkanen should be shopped.

A core of Peterson, Keyonte George, Ace Bailey and Jackson are all 26 or younger. Markkanen, meanwhile, will turn 30 next spring and doesn't fit the timeline of this group. He's also taking a starting spot away from Peterson or Bailey, the two players with the highest ceilings on this team.

A three-year, $149.5 million remaining contract is something contenders can talk themselves into, especially since it only accounts for less than 28 percent of the cap next season and Markkanen is coming off an excellent season (career-high 26.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.0 steals). His swing rating of plus-10.3 ranked in the 95th percentile among all players, per Cleaning the Glass .

Able to play either forward position at 7'1", Markkanen would be a needed shot of offense for teams like the Golden State Warriors or Detroit Pistons. The Minnesota Timberwolves crave a starting power forward like Markkanen, although a trade would be unlikely without Jaden McDaniels involved.

Yes, the Jazz should be trying to snag a play-in spot in the West next season, but reaching this team's potential is more important. That means big minutes for players like Peterson and Bailey, even if it means trading Markkanen in the process.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Devin Booker is the face of the Phoenix Suns. Dillon Brooks, Mark Williams and Colin Gillespie all signed extensions with the franchise and the Suns traded for Miles Bridges this offseason.

The 24-year-old wing is entering the final guaranteed year of his contract at $36.3 million and has a $36 million player option for 2027-28. He averaged 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and shot 31.3 percent from three for the Suns last season, appearing in just 32 total games due to injury.

Phoenix should absolutely be testing the market for Green, as he's not a good fit alongside Booker in the backcourt. The Suns had a net rating of plus-8.7 (87th percentile) with a backcourt of Gillespie and Booker , compared to just plus-2.8 with Booker and Green (65th percentile). Gillespie's new four-year, $48 million contract will pay him about a third of what Green makes annually.

Booker is a shooting guard who can handle the ball, not a point guard who can shoot. The Suns had a net rating of plus-9.2 when Booker played shooting guard last season. When he was at the point, this number fell to minus-0.7.

Unless Phoenix can mold Green into a super sixth man, a trade may be best for both parties.

Green is a talented scorer and still has plenty of upside, but this is a bad fit.

The Brooklyn Nets could use him as a better version of Cam Thomas as they try to get back to contention. The new-look Los Angeles Clippers are an intriguing fit alongside Darius Garland in the backcourt or the Dallas Mavericks could use some backcourt scoring punch to balance out the roster.

Zion Williamson, PF, New Orleans Pelicans

Zion Williamson used to be one of the hottest names in all of basketball after going No. 1 overall in the 2019 draft.

Injuries and trade rumors surrounded him for years, although now it seems like the basketball world has collectively forgotten about the two-time All-Star.

Williamson has quietly played 62 games or more in two of the last three seasons, averaging 22.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 4.4 assists and shooting 57.9 percent overall during this stretch. He looks to be in the best shape of his NBA career and shot a career-high 74.4 percent from within three feet last season.

The New Orleans Pelicans have had one of the quietest offseasons in the NBA and appear set to run back a roster that won 26 games last year and features several awkward-fitting pieces.

Williamson and Derik Queen both operate inside with the ball in their hands and offer little to no spacing whatsoever. Yves Missi is another former first-round pick who has upside but can't shoot. This frontcourt desperately needs some change.

An NBA front office with a three-point shooting center in need of some star power should be calling about Williamson.

This list includes teams like the Milwaukee Bucks, Los Angeles Clippers and Sacramento Kings, as they can roll the dice on the 26-year-old's talent, especially if he continues to stay in good shape.

articles.body:
Everybody is wondering about where is next for DeWanna Bonner after her Phoenix Mercury buyout.

The Phoenix Mercury agreed to a contract buyout on the remainder of DeWanna Bonner's $500,000 salary, granting the 39-year-old veteran a chance to join a new team.

Currently in her 17th WNBA season, the two-time champion is nearing the end of her legendary career and facing likely retirement after this upcoming postseason run.

Before the buyout, Bonner posted solid contributions for Phoenix, averaging 10.6 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists across 27 minutes per game, so she'll be a handy pickup for any challenging team.

DeWanna Bonner set to join a championship-chasing team

We already saw Bonner address her potential retirement plans , stating that she still feels like she has plenty in her and the drive to continue.

And it seems as if her main aim is to join a team chasing the championship, as Nate Tibbetts spoke out after DeWanna Bonner and the Mercury agreed to a contract buyout in the WNBA .

He said: "This was done out of respect for DB. This is an opportunity for her to chase a title in possibly her last season. Everything happened on great terms, and she's always gonna be part of the Mercury organization… It was different this morning telling my staff that this was going to happen. It was probably different for our team finding out this morning, but this is part of professional sports: it's change, and we've been through a lot."

The Atlanta Dream stand out as a top landing spot due to available cap room and a clear frontcourt fit, but other potential suitors pursuing depth for a title run include the New York Liberty and Las Vegas Aces .

articles.title: Kyle Singler pleads for help from Duke, Coach K in latest concerning social media video
articles.summary: The former Duke star addressed his former college and coach in a troubling social media post on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Former Duke star Kyle Singler has faced troubling issues since retiring from professional basketball, and that only continued with a disturbing series of videos on Tuesday night.

Singler posted three videos on Instagram pleading for help from former Duke coach Mike Krzyzewski and the Duke community, as he is concerned for his life and finances. This marks the third time since 2024 that Singler, who was arrested last year, has posted a concerning set of videos on social media.

Singler claims that he's been turned down by people in his life, so he hopes that the videos can make a difference. Here's why the former Duke star is asking for help.

Kyle Singler pleads for help from Duke, Coach K

On Tuesday night, Singler posted three videos on social media pleading for help, especially from former Duke coach Mike Krzyzewski, who coached Singler in college from 2007 to 2011. Singler claims that he is at risk of being homeless and needs someone to help get him back on the right track.

"Man, Coach K has set me up," Singler said ."Set me up, man. I have no power. I have no house. I've reached out to coach and everybody has turned the other way. I've reached out to coach and he has fully dismissed the message. You guys are cutting my power off, breaking into my house, stealing money, ruining my life. I reached out to Coach K and all he did was sit me on the bench. Thanks, man. Is that what we're doing at that school, sending people down, teaching them up? Cool beans, man...Coach, where you at? Help a brother out. Thought we were on the same team, man."

Singler also accused Duke of still asking him for money despite his financial issues, as he said in one of the videos that his assets have been frozen.

"Coach, man, I've reached out to you many times and shared with you where I'm at, and you've just been deflective," he said. "Leaving people in the dust. I don't respect it. You got a player that's been traded, baby."

What else did Kyle Singler say in social media video

Singler's three-video rant also included him claiming that people were trying to kill him and that he continues to be targeted in crimes in the Oklahoma area.

"I'm out in Oklahoma, I go out walking the street, I get pulled, I get arrested, I get f–king checked, I get kicked out of restaurants," Singler said . "I can't even live anymore. Can't even say, 'Hey, how's it going?' without confrontation...I'm stuck at my house and I can't leave, I feel imprisoned. Where we at? Leaving people stranded. I've tried to share messages about where we're at and back home I got people, my friends, family, devastated and gone, died, and again my life's on the line "Reached out to Coach K," Singler said "And all he did is sit me on the bench."

It's not entirely clear what Singler meant when he referenced Coach K sitting him "on the bench." The crux of Singler's videos, however, was targeted at both Duke and Krzyzewski, but they still painted a picture of what the former basketball player is dealing with now.

Singler last played in the NBA in 2018 and has dealt with trouble in the past few years. In 2024, Singler posted a different series of videos claiming he was fearful for his life every day.

"I have been mistreated and abused, neglected, made into a mental example," he said at the time . "And I fear for my life every day. And people in my community make me look out as if I'm going to be someone that's going to be a problem and make things difficult for people when I'm only trying to be helpful."

Then, in October of 2025, Singler was arrested for allegedly assaulting and threatening his girlfriend in a domestic dispute. A few months later, he posted another series of Instagram videos pleading for help and claiming he's being targeted.

"I don't feel safe," he said. "I've got people in my life taking my money — this is a message to everybody in my life who has been messing with me. My child is being sexually, physically, emotionally, spiritually abused. Shame on everybody that knows me that's not helping, not intervening."

Singler is 38 years old but hasn't played professional basketball since he was 31. The former Duke star last played in the NBA for the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2018, but did have a stint playing overseas in 2018 and 2019.

articles.title: Makoundou, décimo fichaje del Barça: "No está mal empezar de cero, y construirlo todo desde el principio"
articles.standfirst: El nuevo ala-pívot azulgrana cuenta sus primeros días en conjunto azulgrana
articles.summary: El nuevo ala-pívot azulgrana cuenta sus primeros días en conjunto azulgrana
articles.body: El ala-pívot francés Yoan Makoundou, una de las diez caras nuevas del Barça esta temporada, ha asegurado este miércoles que puede aportar al conjunto azulgrana "atletismo y defensa", dos de sus principales virtudes y con las que espera contribuir a que el equipo firme una buena temporada. "Puedo aportar atletismo, defensa, me gusta proteger el rebote, tengo cierta habilidad desde el tiro. Creo que puedo aportar en muchos aspectos", ha afirmado el interior francés en unas declaraciones difundidas por el club catalán. Makoundou, que llega procedente del Mónaco y acumula experiencia en la Euroliga, la Eurocopa y la Liga de Campeones, ya ha completado sus primeras sesiones de trabajo junto a otros recién llegados como Josh Nebo, Agus Ubal, Tyrese Martin, Stanley Umude y Justin Robinson. Una primera toma de contacto que le ha permitido empezar a conocer a sus nuevos compañeros. "Me siento muy bien, emocionado, con ganas de empezar a trabajar y ponernos a punto con los nuevos compañeros", ha explicado el francés, de 2,07 metros, que ha firmado un contrato por dos temporadas, hasta el 30 de junio de 2028. El ala-pívot también ha recordado las conversaciones mantenidas con el club catalán antes de cerrar su incorporación. "Tuvimos oportunidad de hablar, fue una llamada muy interesante, agradable, llegamos a un buen entendimiento. Me explicaron cómo yo podía ayudar al equipo y cómo ellos me podían ayudar a mí. Confiamos en que todo saldrá bien", ha señalado. El francés ha valorado especialmente la posibilidad de empezar a construir el equipo desde cero junto a una plantilla con numerosos jugadores nuevos. "No está mal empezar de cero, tener que conocernos con los nuevos compañeros, construirlo todo desde el principio. Creo que es positivo", ha apuntado. Su estreno ante la afición azulgrana llegará el próximo 24 de septiembre, con motivo del partido inaugural de la Euroliga frente al Anadolu Efes, que además servirá para celebrar la fiesta del centenario de la sección. "Será mi primera vez en el Palau Blaugrana, estoy seguro de que todo irá bien y esperamos hacer levantar a la afición de sus asientos con los mates y otras acciones. Estoy deseando jugar allí y sentir el ambiente", ha concluido.

articles.title: Michael Jordan's Iconic Custom Ferrari 550 Maranello to Be Sold at Auction, Could Fetch $1M+
articles.summary: A Ferrari once owned by the legendary Michael Jordan is set to hit the auction block next month, and it could sell for an eye-popping price.
articles.body:
A Ferrari once owned by the legendary Michael Jordan is set to hit the auction block next month, and it could sell for an eye-popping price.

Per The Athletic's Benjamin Burrows , Jordan's 1997 Ferrari 550 Maranello disappeared from public view after he sold it in December 2002. The vehicle was rediscovered by the supercar dealership Curated, which is bringing it to auction in partnership with the marketplace Joopiter. It reportedly carries a pre-sale estimate of $700,000-$1.3 million, and bidding runs from Sept. 15 to Sept. 30.

Jordan was famously seen driving his Ferrari after Game 6 of the 1997 NBA Finals, when he won his fifth NBA championship with the Chicago Bulls.

The Ferrari was modified with custom seat tracks and padding density to fit the 6'6" Jordan. Nike designer Tinker Hatfield later used the vehicle as the inspiration for the Air Jordan 14.

In addition to Jordan's Ferrari, Joopiter is also selling the jersey he wore during Game 3 of the 1998 NBA Finals. Burrows noted the item has a pre-sale estimate of $10-$15 million.

articles.body: ESPN reporter Tim MacMahon took a random shot at Enes Kanter Freedom while breaking down Klay Thompson’s move to the Miami Heat. MacMahon was breaking down how Thompson fit with the Heat before taking an unprompted jab at Freedom. "You got to protect (Thompson) defensively now, and instead of being a guy who you can put on the other team’s best perimeter scorer, but the Heat are as desperate for shooting as Enes Kanter is for attention," MacMahon said on a recent episode of ESPN’s "Brain Windhorst & The Hoop Collective." Upon hearing MacMahon’s comment, Windhorst immediately said, "Oh no." However, MacMahon continued his analysis without dwelling on his Freedom comment. "And so like Klay, on a low-cost, relatively low-cost deal does make sense," MacMahon said. Freedom has been in the news after he was kicked out of Wintrust Arena on Sunday night after an altercation with Sky player Natasha Cloud during the Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky game. During the third quarter of the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Sky at Wintrust Arena, Cloud began barking at Freedom, who was sitting courtside. Freedom then stepped toward the floor and yelled back at Cloud with his arms spread, with security quickly intervening and ushering Freedom out. Kanter later spoke to OutKick about the incident. "Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’ "And I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her.’ And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me, and literally I just got up, and then I was like, ‘I’m just here to protect women, and that’s all.’" Kanter, who recently declared himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft, attended the game wearing a shirt that defined what a woman is, something the league itself has not yet seemed to answer. Following the incident with Cloud, Sky owner Michael Alter barred Kanter from the arena. "He has demonstrated to us, unequivocally, that he has the potential to be a threat," Alter said, via ESPN. Sky officials explained to OutKick later Tuesday that Wintrust Arena security, NBA security and Chicago police determined Freedom to be a threat. The determination came when Freedom opened his arms, pointed toward Cloud and stepped toward the court, according to the officials. "My letter to Commissioner Engelbert makes one point: rules are rules, and the WNBA must enforce them fairly," Freedom said. "I followed the league’s rules, yet I was ejected without the required warning while Natasha Cloud faced no consequences for berating a spectator — a clear violation of league policy.
