articles.title: Warriors Unveil 'Nellie' Uniform Band Honoring Late Don Nelson in Photo Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors announced Wednesday that they will wear a band on their uniforms throughout the 2026-27 season to honor late Hall of Fame coach Don Nelson.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors announced Wednesday that they will wear a band on their uniforms throughout the 2026-27 season to honor late Hall of Fame coach Don Nelson.

Located on the shoulder of the players' jerseys, the band will read "Nellie," which was Nelson's nickname.

Nelson, who spent 11 seasons as the Warriors' head coach over two separate stints from 1988 to 1995 and 2006 to 2010, died on Aug. 9 at the age of 86.

During his time with the Warriors, Nelson compiled a 422-443 regular-season record, and he led the team to the playoffs on five occasions.

From 1989 to 1991, Nelson's Warriors teams were among the most exciting in the NBA thanks to the trio of Tim Hardaway, Chris Mullin and Mitch Richmond, who are all Hall of Famers and were known collectively as Run TMC.

Nelson never made it past the second round of the playoffs during his first run with Golden State, but he helped lead the Warriors to one of the biggest upsets in postseason history during his second stint.

In 2007, the Warriors were the No. 8 seed in the Western Conference and they were heavy first-round underdogs against a Dallas Mavericks team that went 67-15.

However, Nelson's Warriors shocked the Mavs, marking the first time in NBA history that a No. 8 seed eliminated a No. 1 seed in a seven-game playoff series.

All told, Nelson was an NBA head coach for 31 seasons with the Warriors, Milwaukee Bucks, Mavericks and New York Knicks.

His 1,335 career regular-season wins are the second-most by a head coach in NBA history, and he also ranks 15th on the all-time playoff wins list with 75 despite having never won a championship as a coach.

Nelson was a three-time NBA Coach of the Year, though, and he won five championships as a player during his 11-year run with the Boston Celtics from 1965 to 1976.

Nelson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012, just two years after the end of his coaching career.

The Warriors will open 2026-27 regular season play on Oct. 21 when they go on the road to face the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Bennedict Mathurin, Pelicans Reportedly Agree to Contract amid Clippers Qualifying Offer Rumors
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans and ex-Los Angeles Clippers wing Bennedict Mathurin have agreed to a two-year, $16 million deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans and ex-Los Angeles Clippers wing Bennedict Mathurin have agreed to a two-year, $16 million deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Clippers previously tendered Mathurin a qualifying offer, making him a free agent. Insider Jake Fischer reported Wednesday that the Clippers "haven't yet withdrawn" the qualifying offer but "will indeed work with Mathurin" to facilitate his move to New Orleans.

The 6'5" Mathurin averaged a career-high 17.6 points on 43.0 percent shooting (31.5 percent from three), 5.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 54 games (25 starts) last season.

The Indiana Pacers selected the former Arizona star with the sixth overall pick in the 2022 NBA draft. The 24-year-old played three-plus seasons in Indiana and helped the Pacers reach the 2024 Eastern Conference Finals and the 2025 NBA Finals.

On Feb. 5, 2026, the Pacers traded him to the Clippers in a multi-player and multi-pick deal that, of note, sent center Ivica Zubac to Indiana. Mathurin served as the Clippers' sixth man, averaging 17.4 PPG.

The Pelicans and Mathurin were initially linked on July 28. NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that New Orleans continued to show interest in the former University of Arizona star, to the point that the Pels and Mathurin had "recent dialogue." However, it wasn't clear at the time if a deal was close.

In the end, a deal was reached, culminating in a long-standing pursuit, per Charania.

New Orleans certainly likes Mathurin's potential as showcased during his four NBA seasons, and now he might be a core piece of its future.

articles.title: Bennedict Mathurin reportedly agrees to 2-year, $16 million deal with Pelicans
articles.summary: Mathurin has averaged 16.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game over the first four seasons of his career.
articles.body:
Restricted free-agent wing Bennedict Mathurin , who was traded to the Los Angeles Clippers from the Indiana Pacers last season, has agreed to a two-year, $16 million contract with the New Orleans Pelicans , per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal comes with a player option, according to Charania, who also reported Wednesday that Mathurin's representatives approached the Clippers about withdrawing his $8.8 million qualifying offer and that Mathurin eyed flexibility and the earliest path to unrestricted free agency next summer.

Mathurin, 24, has averaged 16.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 28.6 minutes per game over the first four seasons of his career. He has shot 44.2% from the field and 83.8% from the free-throw line on more than five attempts per game.

That ability to get to the charity stripe has been one of the calling cards of the swingman's game since the Pacers selected him with the sixth overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft. Among 199 players who have logged at least 5,000 total minutes over the past four seasons, Mathurin ranks 13th in free-throw attempt rate ; among guards and wings, he ranks fifth , behind only Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , James Harden , Deni Avdija and Trae Young .

Mathurin brings a physical, north-south slashing game from the perimeter, averaging seven or more drives to the basket per game in each of his four pro seasons and taking 60% or more of his shots in the lane, according to Cleaning the Glass . It's a relentless approach that can produce big games, like the career-high-tying 38 points in 34 minutes he poured in for the Clippers against the Denver Nuggets back in February:

On the nights when Mathurin's converting up close, getting to the line and knocking down his jumpers, he looks like the kind of 1-on-1 shot-creating scorer that a team can build its offense around. Those nights haven't come as often as you'd like, though: Mathurin has shot 63% inside of three feet, 41% on midrange jumpers and 33.6% of his 3-point attempts — all below league-average effectiveness.

That errant shot-making, combined with a negative career assist-to-turnover ratio (500 helpers to 502 cough-ups), low block and steal rates for a wing — especially one with Mathurin's athleticism and positional size, at 6-foot-5 and 210 pounds with a 6-9 wingspan — have led to the Montreal native grading out poorly by a number of advanced metrics, including estimated plus-minus, box plus-minus, value over replacement player, player efficiency rating, win shares per 48 minutes and DARKO daily plus-minus.

The eye test, though, has shown Mathurin's physicality and capacity to generate free throws can make him a valuable player in some postseason contexts — most notably during the Pacers' 2025 NBA Finals run, during which he often shined off the bench, scoring 23 points in 27 minutes in Game 3 against Cleveland , 20 points in 13 minutes in Game 4 against New York, 27 points in 23 minutes in Game 3 against Oklahoma City , and 24 points with 13 rebounds in Game 7 of the Finals, with Indiana needing some offensive spark after Tyrese Haliburton ruptured his Achilles tendon.

The collision of that statistical résumé with those playoff performances has made questions surrounding what Mathurin's ideal NBA role would look like — and what to pay him to perform it — somewhat thorny.

Mathurin's isolation-heavy, ball-dominant style made him an at-times awkward fit in Indiana's ball- and player-movement-heavy offensive scheme. With the Pacers changing course following Haliburton's injury and the trade of center Myles Turner , they didn't reach agreement on an extension of Mathurin's rookie-scale contract heading into his fourth season, ticketing him for restricted free agency come the summer — though they did begin the 2025-26 campaign with Mathurin in the starting lineup.

After opening the season with a pair of big offensive performances against the Thunder and Grizzlies, Mathurin sprained the big toe on his right foot, sidelining him for 11 games. He'd return in mid-November, averaging 16.6 points while shooting just 45.7% on 2-pointers over the next month and a half before once again suffering an injury — this time, a sprained right thumb — that put him back on the shelf for another 11 games.

Shortly after his return to the lineup, Mathurin found himself on the move, traded to the Clippers along with center Isaiah Jackson and three draft picks — including a protected 2026 first-rounder that wound up turning into No. 5 overall pick Keaton Wagler — in the deal that brought Ivica Zubac to Indiana. Granted the freedom to cook in Tyronn Lue's second unit, Mathurin posted career highs in usage rate, points, rebounds and assists per 36 minutes and PER over the final 26 games in L.A.

The Clippers went 15-11 with Mathurin in the lineup during the regular season, finishing at 42-40 and in ninth place in the Western Conference. They fell to the Golden State Warriors in the play-in tournament, 126-121, with Mathurin scoring a team-high 23 points on 7-for-11 shooting in 30 minutes off the bench.

articles.title: Joey, Jesse Buss Join New Padres Ownership Group Amid Attempted Sale of Lakers Stake
articles.summary: Longtime Los Angeles Lakers executives Joey and Jesse Buss are purchasing a stake in the San Diego Padres.
articles.body:
Longtime Los Angeles Lakers executives Joey and Jesse Buss are purchasing a stake in the San Diego Padres.

The Buss brothers are joining a Padres ownership group led by Kwanza Jones and José E. Feliciano, they announced Wednesday (h/t ESPN's Dave McMenamin ).

The investment is being made by Buss Sports Capital, a sports investment firm launched by the Buss brothers in September 2025.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

The Padres sale was recently approved by MLB at a record valuation of $3.9 billion.

The news comes after ESPN's Shams Charania reported Aug. 17 the Buss family trust had decided to sell their minority stake in the Lakers after a majority vote.

The Athletic's Dennis Lin initially reported in July that Joey and Jesse Buss were interested in minority ownership of the Padres.

The brothers were fired from their previous front office positions with the Lakers early in the 2025-26 season, they told Charania last November.

Their previous roles included work in the scouting department tied with bringing in players including Austin Reaves, according to Charania.

The Lakers are in the midst of a pending sale to an ownership group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at a record valuation of $12.5 billion, which was reported earlier this month by ESPN's Ramona Shelburne .

The move, which has yet to be officially approved by the NBA, came less than two years after the Buss family sold their majority stake in the franchise to Mark Walter at a franchise valuation of $10 billion.

The Buss family retained a 17.8 percent stake in the Lakers after the second sale, per Charania.

The Athletic's Sam Amick reported Jeanie Buss, who served as team governor after the franchise's sale to Walter, has opposed the vote to sell her family's stake in the team.

Iger told the California Post 's Khobi Price before the Buss family voted to sell the minority stake he had "every intention to honor the agreement" retaining Jeanie as the Lakers' team governor, although he added "if things change, they'll change."

MLB owners unanimously approved the sale of the Padres to Jones and Feliciano from the Seidler family.

The Seidler family was part of the ownership group that purchased the Padres at an $800 million valuation in 2012. John Seidler had taken over as chairman in 2025 after his brother, former owner Peter Seidler, died in 2023.

The Padres are in the running for an NL Wild Card spot. A trip to the postseason would mark the first time in franchise history the Padres have made three consecutive playoff runs.

articles.title: Caitlyn Jenner backs Enes Kanter Freedom’s WNBA ‘peace summit’ proposal
articles.summary: Caitlyn Jenner has stepped directly into the center of the WNBA’s ongoing eligibility battle. Enes Kanter has offered the WNBA a formal peace deal proposing...
articles.body:
Caitlyn Jenner has stepped directly into the center of the WNBA's ongoing eligibility battle.

Enes Kanter has offered the WNBA a formal peace deal proposing a sit-down summit to establish explicit policy definitions regarding biological women in the league. And, to give the meeting authority, Kanter named Olympic icon Caitlyn Jenner as his preferred moderator, citing her status as a legendary athlete to lead the dialogue.

While Jenner has publicly backed his overarching cause, arguing the league needs firm, clear eligibility rules, the WNBA is almost certain to ignore the offer. League officials have already dismissed these tactics as bad-faith distractions and hold zero interest in negotiating policy on his terms.

However, that won't stop Jenner and Kanter from trying, as they look to build up a bit of a partnership.

Caitlyn Jenner sends messages of support on text to Enes Kanter

It's crazy the amount of eyes that the whole debate has brought onto the WNBA , Caitlyn Jenner included.

And Jenner is more than willing to step in and assist Enes Kanter 's cause, offering to help moderate the dialogue with league officials.

Kanter shared the texts between himself and Jenner when talking to Benny Johnson: "I actually had a conversation with her last night. She said, 'Listen, I love what you're doing. Whatever you're doing, just count me in. I will do anything to help.' I asked, 'Listen, we might offer them a peace summit—would you be okay to moderate it?' She said, 'Amen.'"

articles.title: Caitlin Clark has 'a Michael Jordan mindset' and is 'Taylor Swift in tennis shoes'
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark had her fifth career 30-point-plus, 10-assist-plus performance against the Chicago Sky. The rest of WNBA history includes four such games.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark drives much of the interest in the WNBA , but does that require to speak about every controversy the league faces?

Fox Sports commentator Colin Cowherd compares her to one of the biggest names in basketball history.

"She's Steph Curry (in playing style), but with kind of a Michael Jordan mindset," Cowherd said. "All business, all basketball, has no opinion or comment on the controversies."

Clark spoke about on-court issues — primarily officiating — early in the season. But she has steered clear of social issues, notably whether transgender women should be allowed in women's sports .

Cowherd said Clark's presence "is a singular reason that the league is in a much better spot financially," noting a new collective bargaining agreement that pays players much more and offers better travel conditions, and a lucrative TV deal.

The third-year player had her fifth 30-point-plus, 10-assist-plus performance last weekend against the Chicago Sky . The rest of WNBA history includes four such games.

Indiana Fever photos of Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham vs. Chicago Sky

However, he added: "The path to growth is always through discomfort," identifying UFC from a decade ago, several pro sports dynasties and current college sports that benefit financially from offseason and off-the-field/court/octagon controversies.

"The WNBA was growing and the reason it was growing was because the quality is pretty good," he said. "The North Star of the league's growth — private jets, new TV deal, packed arenas — Taylor Swift in tennis shoes is Caitlin Clark . She's not driving the controversy although she's surrounded with it. But like Michael Jordan, she is all business."

Caitlin Clark averages 22.1 points (third in the WNBA), 8.3 assists (first) and 3.8 rebounds per game. She has made 45% of her shots, 36.8% of her 3-pointers and 83.8% of her free throws.
